cf.title: Reject incompatible options specified with VACUUM ONLY_DATABASE_STATS

input.subject: Reject incompatible options specified with VACUUM ONLY_DATABASE_STATS

verdict_reasoning: The goal is sound: `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PARALLEL 1)` succeeds against the documented rule. Two fixable points remain. maintenance-fit-2 asks why v3 also rejects explicitly disabled options, which the current docs wording ("enabled") allows. maintenance-fit-1 notes that per-option flags accept a future option unless its author remembers to set the flag. Neither needs a different proposal.

brief.title: Reject any option except VERBOSE with VACUUM ONLY_DATABASE_STATS
brief.problem: The docs say ONLY_DATABASE_STATS allows no other option except VERBOSE, but the current check looks only at option bits. So `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PARALLEL 1)` succeeds while `SKIP_LOCKED` fails, which can confuse users.
brief.proposed_design: The patch records during parsing which incompatible options were given, following the "_given" pattern in publicationcmds.c and foreigncmds.c. It rejects any explicitly specified option other than VERBOSE, whatever its value, including explicitly disabled options and explicit PROCESS_MAIN and PROCESS_TOAST. Implicit defaults stay allowed.
user_visible_surface: VACUUM ONLY_DATABASE_STATS now errors when given PARALLEL, INDEX_CLEANUP, TRUNCATE or BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT.
VACUUM ONLY_DATABASE_STATS now errors on explicitly disabled options and on explicit PROCESS_MAIN or PROCESS_TOAST, which were accepted before.
The vacuum.sgml text changes from "no other option may be enabled" to "no other option may be specified".
author_claims: The current behaviour does not match the documentation.
PARALLEL, INDEX_CLEANUP, TRUNCATE and BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT have no effect with ONLY_DATABASE_STATS.
A presence-based check fits the generic error message, like the FULL with BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT check.
The "_given" pattern scales better to future options than a loop over option names.
brief.thread_state: Jim Jones reviewed it, posted an alternative v2 that loops over option names in ExecVacuum, then agreed with keeping the v1 approach. v3 adds a test for `VERBOSE false`; no committer has replied.
unclear: The thread does not discuss whether rejecting previously accepted commands, such as explicit PROCESS_TOAST false, could break existing scripts or tools.
The thread does not say whether the fix should be back-patched or only go into the target version 20.
The thread does not say if vacuumdb or other clients pass options together with ONLY_DATABASE_STATS.

prior_attempts.title: COPY: validate option presence rather than option values
prior_attempts.what_is_different: The same author proposed presence-based option validation for COPY and withdrew it; no reason is recorded. This proposal covers one VACUUM option and points to a documentation mismatch.

objections.title: Rejecting explicit PROCESS_TOAST/PROCESS_MAIN reverses a deliberate tolerance
objections.failure_scenario: A maintenance script runs `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PROCESS_TOAST false)` and works today. After the upgrade to 20 it fails with an error, and the operator finds out when a cron job or tool reports failure after the upgrade.
objections.argument: The current code has the comment "don't require people to turn off PROCESS_TOAST/MAIN explicitly" (quoted in message #2), so accepting these options looks intentional. The patch rejects them anyway, and also rejects explicitly disabled options that are harmless. No message gives a user report that asks for the stricter rule, and none weighs the compatibility cost or says whether vacuumdb sends such combinations. Fixing PARALLEL, INDEX_CLEANUP, TRUNCATE and BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT does not require breaking these no-op forms.
objections.author_must_show: Why must explicitly disabled options and explicit PROCESS_TOAST/PROCESS_MAIN be rejected, when rejecting only the options that have effects would fix the reported bug?

critic.reasoning: The docs today say no other option may be "enabled", so explicitly disabled options are accepted as documented, and v3 changes that. The thread does not weigh this cost, and a check on enabled options would fix the reported cases.

objections.title: Denylist of given options fails open for future VACUUM options
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new VACUUM option and its author does not set the new conflict flag in the parser. Then `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, NEWOPT)` is accepted and silently ignored, the same bug this patch fixes. Nothing fails at build time or in the existing tests, so a user finds out when the documented rule does not hold.
objections.argument: The brief and commit message say the patch tracks the incompatible options that were given, which is a denylist. The allowlist loop in message #2 rejects any new option by default and fails closed. Message #4 says both approaches need the same care, but only the denylist needs every future option author to remember ONLY_DATABASE_STATS. Message #3 argues the "_given" pattern scales better, but the publicationcmds.c and foreigncmds.c cases mainly detect duplicate options and do not enforce an allowlist.
objections.author_must_show: When someone adds a VACUUM option next year without touching this check, what makes ONLY_DATABASE_STATS reject it, or which test fails?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 names a conflict flag that the parser sets per option, so a new option that does not set it is accepted. Message #4 says both approaches need the same care, but the loop over option names rejects unknown options by default.

refuted.title: Rejecting explicitly disabled options breaks commands accepted since the feature began
refuted.failure_scenario: A maintenance script or tool runs `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PROCESS_TOAST false)` or `INDEX_CLEANUP off`, which works today and does nothing harmful. After upgrading to the release with this patch, the job fails with an error. The operator finds out when the nightly job reports a failure.
refuted.argument: The existing code is commented "don't require people to turn off PROCESS_TOAST/MAIN explicitly" (diff in message #2), so accepting these options was a deliberate choice. Under v3, explicitly disabled and no-op options become errors, and the thread does not discuss who already sends them. [P1] records reviewers declining to break a long-standing behaviour that nobody had complained about. The thread cites no user report, and a value-based check would fix the PARALLEL 1 case without rejecting no-op settings.
refuted.author_must_show: Do vacuumdb or common tools send other options with ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, and why reject no-op values such as PROCESS_TOAST false instead of only enabled ones?

precedents.title: pg_stat_database update stats_reset only by pg_stat_reset

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. The quoted code comment covers implicit defaults, which v3 still allows, and [P1] concerned a behaviour that its code comment and commit message recorded as intentional.

refuted.title: Rejects commands that were accepted, with no evidence they caused harm
refuted.failure_scenario: A maintenance script or tool builds one option list for every VACUUM and runs `vacuum (only_database_stats, process_toast false, index_cleanup auto)`. After upgrade to 20 the command fails with "cannot be specified with other VACUUM options", and the nightly job stops. The operator finds out from failed cron output or from age(datfrozenxid) alarms.
refuted.argument: The commit message says the patch rejects explicitly disabled options and explicit PROCESS_MAIN/PROCESS_TOAST that are accepted today, and these do no harm. The current code comment says users should not be required to turn PROCESS_TOAST/MAIN off explicitly, so an explicit `false` was tolerated by design. The thread reports no user who was hurt by the lenient check, and the CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, which suggests a back-patch the thread never discusses. A committer would likely ask whether rejecting only options that request work would close the documentation gap without breaking valid spellings.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing callers, including vacuumdb run against a newer server, pass other options with ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, and why should explicit no-op values such as `process_toast false` now fail?

precedents.title: pg_stat_database update stats_reset only by pg_stat_reset

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. The CommitFest entry targets version 20, so no back-patch is proposed, and the code comment covers implicit defaults, not an explicit `false`.

refuted.title: Rejecting explicit 'off' options breaks working commands with no reported need
refuted.failure_scenario: A maintenance script runs `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PROCESS_TOAST false)` or `(ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PARALLEL 0)`, which succeed today. After upgrading to the release with this patch, the job fails with "ONLY_DATABASE_STATS cannot be specified with other VACUUM options". The operator finds out when the scheduled job errors after the upgrade.
refuted.argument: The thread cites no user who was confused or harmed. The case in message #1 was found by reading the docs, and the accepted options have no effect. The patch rejects options that are explicitly disabled or explicitly set to defaults, so the only users who notice are the ones whose commands stop working. A committer would likely ask why the docs, or only the options with a real effect, should not be changed instead, as in [P1], where reviewers kept long-standing behaviour that nobody had complained about.
refuted.author_must_show: Which user reports show harm from the current behaviour, and why is a docs change or a value-based check not enough for them?

precedents.title: pg_stat_database update stats_reset only by pg_stat_reset

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2 for the compatibility point. The request for user reports is weak here, because `vacuum (ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PARALLEL 1)` succeeds against the documented rule, and [P1] concerned a behaviour recorded as intentional.

touch_points.reason: VACUUM option lists that are accepted today, such as `(ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, PROCESS_TOAST false)`, become errors; no new syntax is added.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix with target version 20, and the patch makes previously accepted commands fail.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Each future VACUUM option must set the conflict flag in the parser, or ONLY_DATABASE_STATS accepts it silently.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why must explicitly disabled options and explicit PROCESS_TOAST or PROCESS_MAIN be rejected, when rejecting only enabled options would fix the reported cases?
Do vacuumdb or other known clients send any option other than VERBOSE together with ONLY_DATABASE_STATS?
When someone adds a VACUUM option without touching this check, what makes ONLY_DATABASE_STATS reject it, or which test fails?
Is the change meant for version 20 only, given that the entry is tagged Bugfix?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the VACUUM command code and its option parsing would have to own it; none has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a user-visible behaviour change in version 20: some VACUUM commands that worked start to fail. The liability is small and limited to option validation in vacuum.c.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the review within two days and posted v3 with the requested test.

priority.reason: The patch is about 10 KiB, touches only vacuum.c, the VACUUM reference page and regression tests, and already has one reviewer. Few users combine other options with ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, and the two open points can be settled in the thread.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so how the parser sets the conflict flag and whether a shared struct such as VacuumParams changes are not known. Message #4 was not shown; it may already address the choice between per-option flags and a loop over option names.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_stat_database update stats_reset only by pg_stat_reset
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops pg_stat_reset_single_table_counters and pg_stat_reset_single_function_counters from updating stats_reset in pg_stat_database, so that only a full pg_stat_reset changes it. The author wanted stats_reset to mark the point where all database-level counters, such as xact_commit, were reset.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Resetting the database timestamp on any per-object reset is intentional: the code comment and the 2011 commit message both say so, and nobody had complained since. Reviewers did not want to break an 8-year-old behaviour that monitoring may rely on. A changed stats_reset tells a monitoring tool that some counters in the database were reset, and per-object timestamps would add overhead and make queries more complex. The author agreed and withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree with Daniel that breaking an 8-year-old behavior may not be of
the taste of folks relying on the current behavior, particularly
because we have not had complains about the current behavior being
bad.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump -C Grant statement on create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: When pg_dump is run with -C (emit CREATE DATABASE), it would also emit the database-level GRANT statements (such as GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE), matching what pg_dumpall already produces. The patch makes emitting these grants subject to the existing -x (no privileges) option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread contains only the original report, a reply agreeing it is an oversight, and the patch submission; no review or objection to the patch appears, and the entry was returned with feedback about three months later.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert the commits related to allowing page lock to conflict among parallel group members.
Reverted commit(s): Allow page lock to conflict among parallel group members.; Add assert to ensure that page locks don't participate in deadlock cycle.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts the work done by commits 3ba59ccc89 and 72e78d831a.
Those commits were incorrect in asserting that we never acquire any other
heavy-weight lock after acquring page lock other than relation extension
lock. We can acquire a lock on catalogs while doing catalog look up after
acquring page lock.

This won't impact any existing feature but we need to think some other way
to achieve this before parallelizing other write operations or even
improving the parallelism in vacuum (like allowing multiple workers
for an index).

precedents_retrieved.title: vacuumlo: add test to vacuumlo for test coverage
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a TAP test for vacuumlo to raise its test coverage. The test runs vacuumlo in verbose dry-run mode against a test cluster and checks the output.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not send a revised patch after review, so the entry was returned with feedback. Daniel Gustafsson asked for more scenarios, such as a non-existing database or one with no large objects, and asked the test to use run_command(). Ian Lawrence Barwick noted that the test was not added to meson.build.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:

precedents_retrieved.title: VACUUM Progress Checker
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a way to report the progress of long-running VACUUM commands, such as pages scanned and the current phase, so DBAs can judge whether to wait or abort. The design moved from a shared-preload-library hook to a general per-backend progress-reporting facility in PgBackendStatus, with counter and message update functions, exposed through a pg_stat_vacuum_progress view.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was still being actively reworked when the commitfest closed, so it was returned with feedback and the author was asked to resubmit to the next commitfest. The reporting interface and its counters were not yet settled: reviewers were still asking for a lightweight API that updates a single counter or message, for reporting the current block number, and for finer-grained index-phase reporting, and new review comments arrived on the latest version. In the previous commitfest it had already been returned as not committable, with Michael Paquier questioning the design of the progress facility.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since things are clearly still moving here, I closed it as
returned-with-feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow specifying action when standby encounters incompatible parameter settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, modeled on recovery_target_action, that sets what a standby does when it sees an incompatible parameter change: 'pause' replay (the behavior since 15251c0) or 'shutdown' (the earlier behavior). The use case is automation that adjusts the parameters and restarts the standby without waiting for the pause to be detected.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs objected that the option brings back the shutdown-on-change behavior, which had caused outages for users, and that 15251c0 had removed it to keep standbys available. He argued that orchestration tools should check parameter values on all servers and change them in the right order instead. After this objection the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This patch would undo a very important change - to keep servers available by default and go back to the old behavior for a huge fleet of Postgres databases.

precedents_retrieved.title: history of vacuum / checkpoint runs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add hooks that run after vacuum and checkpoint logging, and keep a history of individual runs that users can query instead of parsing the server log. A proof-of-concept extension stored events in a fixed-size circular buffer in shared memory, and the discussion moved toward a file with a time-based retention limit.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Reviewers discussed buffer size, file storage, retention policy, hook signatures and aggregation, but none of the shown messages objects to the idea. The last shown message is from January 2025 and the entry was withdrawn in November 2025, with no visible reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: clean up create|alter domain stmt incompatiable constraint error case and add regression test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch added broader regression tests for CREATE DOMAIN and ALTER DOMAIN (DefineDomain had low test coverage) and cleaned up error handling for incompatible domain constraints. It replaced the unhelpful "unrecognized constraint subtype" error for generated-column constraints on domains with a clear message, and made ALTER DOMAIN ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... NO INHERIT NOT VALID fail.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was withdrawn because the patch had been folded into a later patch version (v6) in another thread. A reviewer asked whether this separate commitfest entry should therefore be closed. No objection to the content of the patch is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks like this patch is now part of v6 from here [0]. Should we close
[1] CF entry?

precedents_retrieved.title: Block level parallel vacuum
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds parallel workers to VACUUM: each worker scans a range of heap blocks, collects dead tuple locations and reclaims them, and the leader gathers the statistics and updates relfrozenxid. Later versions added progress reporting and a per-table parallel degree for autovacuum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch in November 2017 because it depended on a separate extension lock patch, and he proposed coming back once those root problems were addressed. A regression failure ("cache lookup failed for relation" from DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE) was also still unexplained. The first round in 2016 was returned for lack of activity, after early tests showed index vacuum slowing down with more workers because of cleanup lock contention on index buffers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So I propose to mark this patch as
returned with feedback for now, and come back to it once the root
problems are addressed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reject concurrent sequence refreshes".
Reverted commit(s): Reject concurrent sequence refreshes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f38afa4abb04e85530c94b88daf11c089375daca.

That commit fixed a race that could leave stale sequence values on the
subscriber after 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. It did so by
raising an ERROR during 'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'
whenever a sequence synchronization worker was already running for the
subscription.

That approach caused intermittent buildfarm failures, because the existing
tests did not ensure the sequencesync worker had stopped before executing
'ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES'. While discussing how to fix
the tests, we concluded that blocking the command while a sequencesync
worker is running is inconvenient for users. So we will fix the original
race differently in a follow-up commit.

roaster_notes.note: [P19] records no reason, so it supports no objection. The core fix of rejecting enabled PARALLEL, INDEX_CLEANUP, TRUNCATE and BUFFER_USAGE_LIMIT draws no objection from the precedents.
The SQL surface itself adds no keyword or syntax. The only concern from this angle is the stricter acceptance of option lists that were valid before.

The proposal changes only how VACUUM validates its options when it parses them, plus one doc sentence and regression tests. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, replication or wire protocol change. The code is not shown, so it is not known whether a shared struct such as VacuumParams changes, which would matter for extension ABI only if the fix were back-patched; the target is version 20.

The patch only tightens option validation for VACUUM ONLY_DATABASE_STATS. It changes which commands raise an error and adds no new capability, privilege path, exposed data or resource use. A user who could run the command before cannot do or see more after it, so there is no security or privilege aspect to object to.
There is no hot-path cost, no new dependency, and no new API. The fix fits in core. The concerns are limited to how future options are covered and whether old commands should break.

No existing Postgres feature, contrib module or extension covers this. The patch tightens the error check that ExecVacuum already has for ONLY_DATABASE_STATS, so it changes an existing mechanism instead of adding a second way to do the job. [P19] looks at presence-based option checks for COPY, but its reason for withdrawal is not recorded, and the compatibility of rejecting explicit PROCESS_TOAST false belongs to another angle.
Fixing the mismatch between the docs and the code is reasonable. The objection is about rejecting commands that are harmless and work today, and nobody has asked for that.
